name: Non-negative Matrix Monoid Disguise
description: Maps each link's state pair to a 2x2 matrix with non-negative integer entries. Valid pairs (opposite states) map to the Identity matrix. Invalid pairs (same states) map to matrices with a positive off-diagonal entry. The global footprint is the product of these matrices, required to be the Identity. Because the matrices are non-negative and have 1s on the diagonal, their product can only be the Identity if every factor is the Identity. This forces all pairs to have opposite states, preserving the bipartite coloring requirement. It defeats the model by replacing a simple scalar product with a matrix product over a monoid where the monotonicity of off-diagonal elements is not immediately obvious, preventing the model from using simple prime factorization or bounding arguments to deduce the local condition.
